newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds reversed weakness to end higher while the short end stayed soft at the close.
The December Confederate bond future rallied from the day low of 114.25, helped by technical support, one trader said.
The level was the closest the Dec contract has come to revisiting 114.15, the most recent low set on October 17.
"We had support at (114) 20 and 30 in the Conf futures, an area which held up last week," one Swiss bond dealer said.
Volume was middling, with declines in the short end linked to Swiss franc weakness. Mark/Swiss rose to its highest levels in over a year, closing Friday at 82.90/93 Swiss centimes.
The franc also weakened against the dollar. A weaker franc tends to push Swiss short-term interest rates higher.
On LIFFE, December three-month Euro-Swiss futures ended at day's lows, and at roughly its lowests levels since mid-September.

One New York-based Swiss dealer said the market appeared to have a panic reaction after the Swiss franc's latest drop, but he said the move appeared overdone. "The problem is just that people are scared when mark/swiss goes higher. People believe the Swiss National Bank will abandon its more relaxed policy. That is kind of an over-reaction," he said.
"People need to get used to the 83.00 level on the cross," he said. As soon as that happened, he said short-term rates should edge down again.

Rates at the short end of the market are prone to move higher when selling sets in against the Swiss franc, the trader added, because traders who buy dollars short the franc, and must then borrow francs to place a deposit on the dollar side.

Money market traders said the Swiss National Bank continued to add liquidity to the market in the course of normal daily operations on Friday at the 1-1/2 percent rate, the rate which has been in effect in recent sessions.

The SNB just lowered interest rates on September 26, cutting the discount rate to 1.00 percent from 1.50 percent. It has made clear that it prefers a weaker franc as a means to spur the weak Swiss economy.
Dec Conf futures CONFZ6 up 11 at 114.65.
Dec Comi medium-term bond COMIZ6 up five at 110.10.
Dec Euro Swiss francs FESZ6 down 10 at 98.07.
